The cheapest is the dearest, as the old saying goes. Honestly, I've found that taking an attorney up on their free hour or half hour initial consultation will yield vastly better results than an online forum with anonymous people who at best can only make dubious claims to be knowledgeable attorneys or paralegals. If the problem is serious, then hire a qualified experienced professional. If you don't value your time, energy and money, post your question online and run with what you get.

Agreed, actually speaking with an attorney licensed in your state on your issue during an initial consultation is the absolute best way to get started getting advice. Unfortunately, some people don't even know to do that. Many who face their first legal problem are unaware that many lawyers give free-first consultations and that legal consumers should start making phone calls, lots of 'em, or that local bar associations have referral services and often host free pro-bono sessions by volunteer attorneys on certain days of the week. I believe this sub can help give this basic information and more, depending on who's around to answer. That's my vision of it anyway.
